AI security & offensive-security agents (Black Hat's entire product wave is agent containment — Zero Networks ships just-in-time MFA per agent, Sweet Security blocks rogue agents in live production, Acalvio plants honeytokens inside agentic environments; the Linux Foundation puts SAFE out for RFC as a CVE-equivalent for agent incidents; GitHub's #1 repo is a security skill-router at +2,400)

AI coding agents (HN's #1 story argues models multiply what you already know rather than substituting for it, and the sharpest counter is Anthropic's math researcher prompting 'think really hard, trust yourself'; the 'meat proxy' post names relaying model output unread; SWE-Touch benchmarks coding agents when users touch the code concurrently)

Agentic retrieval & RAG architecture (Fetch-then-Explore splits selection from extraction across a persistent workspace rather than one growing context, shipped beside its own failure-mode diagnosis; Verification Without Sufficiency argues per-chunk relevance is the wrong unit for multi-hop RAG and decomposition repairs it; LATAM's ontology work clarified the airline's own definitions)

Governance as a product line (an ex-Deloitte auditor open-sources the whole SOC 2 method aimed at AI products — the best-performing Show HN of the day; Julius Baer hires an architect whose deliverable is Architecture Decision Records approved at architecture boards; NetHope ships a pre-adoption PESTLE due-diligence guide)

Evaluation gap (execution, outcome and experience named as three different questions an agent can split on — a scheduler that books exactly as instructed but never confirms the timezone; Lyft had to make its simulated customers *worse* because articulate LLM users produced >90% offline pass rates that died in production; LATAM found 95% of 'out of scope' classifications were real needs)

AI coding agents (three of HN's top four are critiques of the practice, not the tools — 'don't be a meat proxy' at 1,804 points on humans relaying unread model output, 'LLMs reward expertise' at 1,354 on leverage scaling with existing skill, and a proposal to retype generated code by hand as forced comprehension; the sharpest line is that the prompt/paste-error/retry loop has been rebranded 'agentic engineering')

Agentic retrieval & RAG architecture (Pinecone's Nexus compiles scattered documents into a knowledge layer agents query directly instead of re-retrieving per call, with KnowQL putting intent, provenance, output shape, confidence and *budget* in one declarative call; HALT makes the stopping decision verification-aware; a companion paper finds most agentic-RAG errors happen before any evidence is retrieved)

Governance as a product line (Anaconda's second acquisition in three weeks buys pre-deployment red-teaming, runtime guardrails and NIST/EU-AI-Act compliance automation — governance bolted onto a distribution platform rather than sold as a service; Stanford's AI Index supplies the demand curve, AI-specific governance roles up 17% and firms with no responsible-AI policy down from 24% to 11%, with implementation still blocked by knowledge gaps at 59%)

Evaluation gap (frontier science benchmarks are being passed by shortcut rather than reasoning, so headline scores overstate capability — which lands the same day as this week's automated-mathematics claims and a benchmark-saturation study on the HN front page; the eval-practice answer is that the bottleneck has moved from writing evals to stopping agents from grading their own homework)

Agentic retrieval / RAG-as-decision-loop (the RAG default is under attack from three sides at once - Sierra's Context Engine compiles what a business knows into a stateful context layer, InsightEmb trains embeddings on action intent rather than surface text, and the vectorless-RAG argument says structured data never needed similarity search; HN's best taxonomy of the day says agentic search today is late-interaction retrieval, a smarter harness, or just grep)

Vendor governance as a business line (governance stopped being a compliance cost and became a product SKU from three directions in one week - Snowflake and Databricks sell the control plane, Anthropic sells real-time DLP inference hooks for Enterprise, and the first Swiss AI-governance JD read end to end turns out to be a legal role: law degree, CIPP/E-CIPM-AIGP, German and English, and not one technical requirement)

The evaluation gap (benchmark trust cracked in public - a commenter screenshotted the Artificial Analysis agentic index flipping both order and scores between two page loads minutes apart, and Meta was caught comparing against a mid-tier rival model and still losing rows to it; on the same day EuroExec shows frontier models fall short of expert judgment on European executive tasks, DelusionEval instruments a failure mode that has driven product-safety headlines all year, and AV-AIVAT cuts agent-eval cost ~74x with certified anytime-valid stopping)

Evaluation gap (the sharpest item of the day is a reproducibility challenge — a commenter screenshots the Artificial Analysis agentic leaderboard flipping both order AND scores between two page loads minutes apart with identical chart copy, Qwen 55.4 vs Opus Max 55.3 then Opus Max 59.2 vs Qwen 58.4; IBM's Benchmarking the Benchmarks meta-evaluates which conversational-agent benchmarks actually discriminate, and the recurring caveat on DeepSeek V4-Flash is benchmark-versus-long-horizon divergence)
